reason_short: opaque-key control: Jev's causal-change predictions depend on the option-key identity
reason: The pre-registered validation control (docs/JEV_OPAQUE_KEY_CONTROL_PROTOCOL.md, rule R2) found that Jev's choices change systematically when the canonical change ids are replaced by opaque keys, beyond run-to-run noise. The pre-registered consequence, and the task instruction, is that a freeze whose causal-change decision runs on canonical ids is not used for the locked benchmark. Aggregate accuracy was preserved (R1), so this is a sensitivity finding, not an accuracy loss; see docs/JEV_OPAQUE_KEY_CONTROL.md.

preserved.note: the sealed configuration, its manifest and every pinned source were not modified

locked_split.note: no locked experiment exists and no locked case was run, counted or previewed

enforcement.note: this record is a declaration. The sealed run_experiment/locked_benchmark do not read it, so the runner would still accept the v1 command. Making verify() refuse a superseded freeze requires editing the sealed locked_benchmark.py; that edit was blocked and is left as a user decision (JEV-036).

reversal: Only by an explicit user decision that is logged in docs/JEV_ISSUE_LOG.md; deleting this record without one would be tampering with the audit trail.
